messages:
anika: noticing weird east-west failures on gpu-backplane in us-west-2. ~1-3% packet loss between GPU pods, some jobs time out. traceroute shows next-hop flipping between rack nodes.

mike: can you paste a traceroute and `ip -6 neigh` / `ip -6 route` from a pod/node? also which CNI (cilium/calico)?

anika: cilium with dual-stack enabled. here's a quick dump from node gpu-rack-12:
```
$ ip -6 neigh show dev eth0
fe80::1a2b:3cff:fe4d:e6a0 dev eth0 lladdr aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01 REACHABLE
fe80::1a2b:3cff:fe4d:e6a0 dev eth0 lladdr aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:02 STALE
```
and route:
```
$ ip -6 route show
2001:db8:10::/64 via fe80::1a2b:3cff:fe4d:e6a0 dev eth0
```
Notice same lladdr alternating between two MACs. traceroute to pod-xyz hops to gpu-rack-12 then suddenly to gpu-rack-08.

raj: that looks like duplicate IPv6 being advertised/assigned -> FIB flips. Any chance IPAM allocated the same IPv6 to two pods? check `kubectl get pods -o wide` IPv6 column.

anika: running: pod-abc (10.0.50.12, 2001:db8:10::7) on gpu-rack-12 and pod-def (2001:db8:10::7) on gpu-rack-08. yep duplicate. didn't expect allocator race. :grimacing:

leah: oof. we saw an allocator race on dual-stack last year in staging. kube-controller-manager loses a lease on IPv6 allocator under high churn if leader election moves. Could be the same.

sam: immediate mitigation: cordon one of the nodes and evict the duplicate pod so only one holder remains. Also flush the neighbour table on nodes: `ip -6 neigh flush all` and restart cilium-agent on the affected nodes to rebuild endpoints.

anika: doing that now. cordoning gpu-rack-08 and evicting pod-def. flushing neighbors on the rack nodes.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0421 — dual-stack IPv6 duplicate allocation causing FIB instability on gpu-backplane. Priority: P2. Assignee: eng-infra oncall.

mike: long-term fix: patch the IPv6 allocator to use stronger leader checks and idempotent allocation (or migrate to cluster-wide IPAM that dedups). Also add a nightly job to scan for duplicate IPs and alert before FIB flips.

raj: we should also consider disabling hardware offloads temporarily on the NICs for affected nodes; sometimes offload + ND flapping results in packets sent to stale MACs. commands: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`.

leah: opened PR to kube-controller-manager: tighten dual-stack allocator lock + better logging (link: https://git.redwood/infraproj/kcm/pull/412). putting a canary patch to staging first.

sam: for this incident, rollout plan: 1) cordon+evict duplicates (done), 2) restart cilium on affected nodes (done), 3) monitor FIB/ND for 30m, 4) if stable, uncordon. also schedule kernel/NIC firmware audit for rack-08/12.

anika: after eviction+restart, neighbors look stable and loss dropped to ~0.1%. keeping watch. thanks all :heart:

mike: add postmortem notes to /incidents and include resource usage spike that preceded allocator race. might be a churn-triggered window.

anika: will write a short postmortem and include commands we ran + timeline. saving outputs in the incident thread.
